decision: Build for the agent-runner side of Hermes Desktop first. Do not build a chat-first app for long learning chats now.
why: Hermes users are agent users. Agent tokens grew from 8% to 76% on OpenRouter in one year. A tangent during a long run pollutes the agent context.
evidence: usage table in README; OpenRouter October 2026 data; Anthropic Economic Index June 2026
result: Counter-argument kept: trees fit long chats (13 rounds median) better than agent sessions (1 prompt median).
who: Claude, on Rohan's instruction to decide independently

decision: Reuse Hermes session.branch (new session with parent_session_id). Do not build our own tree store.
why: Hermes already stores branches, nests them in the sidebar, and exposes session.branch through host.request.
result: Depends on Hermes branching code, which has about 8 open bugs.

decision: First feature is a side chat pane during an agent run. Branch tree pane is second. Judge and concept links are third.
why: Side questions during a run are the pain that agent users have. Feature request #75898 asks for this. No product sends side questions to a cheaper model on purpose.

decision: Route side questions with prompt.submit model_override, or auxiliary.side_question for /btw-style snapshots.
why: Both exist in Hermes. A fixed rule (side question gets the cheap model) is enough. RouteLLM is stale.
result: Not run from a plugin yet. Spike first.

decision: Start with an outline tree in a pane. Add a React Flow graph later.
why: Research shows chat stays primary and trees stay shallow (max depth 2 in CanvasConvo). An outline is cheaper.

decision: Run the judge on post_llm_call in a thread. Call a cheap model through ctx.llm.complete_structured. Store marks in ctx.state keyed by session id and row id.
why: Hermes owns the credentials and the user picks the model. The hook has the history and the reply.
result: Not built. Output shape: topic_shift, new_concepts with spans, branch_title.

decision: A concept-link chip opens the branch for now. It does not scroll to a message.
why: No SDK verb can scroll to a message. The internal timeline-reveal event needs a reach into app markup, which the lint refuses.
result: Ask upstream for a reveal verb.

decision: Park the upstream LSP request() PR. Batch it later with the reveal-verb ask.
why: Rohan moved the work to research. The clone at ~/Projects/hermes-agent broke when the session ended. Open PR #55532 overlaps.
result: Clone left as is, not deleted.

decision: The tree pane shows branch sessions and delegate subagent sessions in one tree. Concept links point at the node where a term was defined.
why: The second research found developers use agents and chatbots at about the same rate (66% and 63%). Hermes stores both kinds as sessions with a parent, so one tree costs little.
evidence: Email from the second agent (2026-11-11, sources not checked); hermes_state_delegate_children.py:13-28; hermes_state_mutation_branch.py:52-104
result: Adopted from the second research. Feature order unchanged.
